sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope
sections.body: This policy defines what constitutes a material change to an AI system operated by {org_name} within {boundary}, and requires re-assessment when one occurs. It operationalizes the re-assessment requirement of Texas SB 1964 Sec. 2054.703(b) for heightened-scrutiny systems, which requires documentation to be refreshed at each material change to the system, its data, or its intended use. Aligned to the statute; not legal advice.

sections.heading: 2. Definition of Material Change and Re-assessment Trigger

questions.prompt: What criteria define a material change to the AI system, its underlying data, or its intended use (for example, model version change, new training data source, expanded decision scope, new consequential-decision use)?
Who is responsible for triggering and completing the re-assessment when a material change occurs?

sections.body: A material change to {system_name} is defined as any of: {material_change_criteria}. When a material change occurs, {reassessment_owner} triggers a re-assessment that refreshes the documented known security risks, performance metrics, and transparency measures before the changed system is placed back into operation. Each re-assessment is recorded and associated with the change that triggered it, so the governed transition is reconstructable.
